title: Why some people are taking anxiety meds on nights out
description:
A series of recent studies suggests that drug use is increasing among Gen Z. Some young people are taking prescription anti-anxiety medications — such as propranolol and pregabalin — without a prescription. They’re buying them online or on the black market, exposing themselves to additional risks.

Jacqui Wakefield, our Global Health Reporter, explains why some young people see these drugs as an alternative to alcohol. They want to reduce social anxiety on a night out and experience a feeling of euphoria, but without the calories and hangover that can come with heavy drinking. We discuss the risks associated with using these drugs without medical supervision, and the potential consequences for young people’s health.

Warning: This episode includes references to suicidal thoughts.

If you are affected by any of the issues discussed in this episode, or are experiencing distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide: www.befrienders.org

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World examines why a growing number of Gen Z young people are substituting alcohol with unprescribed anti-anxiety medications, such as propranolol and pregabalin, on nights out. Global Health Reporter Jacqui Wakefield explains that many individuals purchase these drugs via social media, influencers, or online black and grey markets to alleviate social anxiety, achieve euphoria, and avoid alcohol's calories and hangovers. However, self-medicating without medical supervision—or combining multiple substances ("stacking")—carries severe health risks, including escalating dosage tolerance, drug dependency, physical dangers like slowed heart rate, and severe withdrawal symptoms such as heightened anxiety and suicidal thoughts. While some governments are tightening regulations, experts emphasize that anyone dealing with social anxiety should seek professional medical advice or therapy rather than resorting to unprescribed drugs.
